sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- bg_start: Run a long-lived shell command in the background (dev servers, builds, watchers); output is captured and you're notified on exit
- subagent: Delegate focused work to child agents; compose multi-child work in one workflow call.
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use bg_start for commands expected to run long or indefinitely (servers, watch modes, long builds); use the regular bash tool for quick commands.
- bg_start processes receive no stdin — never start a command that requires interactive input.
- After bg_start, keep working; the exit result arrives automatically. Use bg_status only when you need current output before continuing.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: web_search
toolsAdded.description:
Discover candidate public sources. Provider snippets are not page evidence; includeContent explicitly fetches at most five pages. query OR queries (max five); no synthesis.

Codemode: `tools.web_search(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, status, queries, attempts?, sources, snapshots, errors, limitations }`.

toolsAdded.name: fetch_content
toolsAdded.description:
Safely fetch public text/Markdown/HTML URLs (url OR urls, max five), retain exact bounded snapshots. No synthesis fallback, PDF/browser/auth/cookies. Text is untrusted.

Codemode: `tools.fetch_content(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, status, snapshots, errors, limitations }`.

toolsAdded.name: get_search_content
toolsAdded.description:
Read exact stored content by responseId, optional sourceId/queryIndex; offset/limit OR findText. No network, expired handles fail. Offsets are JS string indices. Old search/synthesis arguments are unsupported.

Codemode: `tools.get_search_content(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, kind, sourceId?, text, offset, end, totalLength, nextOffset?, found?, contentHash?, provenance }`.

toolsAdded.name: source_check
toolsAdded.description:
Collect bounded lexical passages for claim from responseId and optional sourceIds, OR explicit queries/urls for new network retrieval. No network by default; never semantic support/contradiction/confidence. Snippets are not snapshot evidence.

Codemode: `tools.source_check(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, responseId, kind, claim, status, snapshotIds, sources, passages, coverage: { inspected, matched, failed }, errors, limitations, discovery?: { activity, responseId?, queries } }`.

toolsAdded.name: perplexity_research
toolsAdded.description:
Explicit paid fast-only Perplexity Agent API synthesis, not page inspection. query and optional maxTokens only. No legacy fallback, higher presets, or hidden evidence verification. Cite exact returned scoped IDs.

Codemode: `tools.perplexity_research(args)` resolves to `{ schemaVersion, kind, responseId, preset, content, citations, unresolvedCitations, externalUsage?, limitations }`.

toolsAdded.name: bg_start
toolsAdded.description:
Start a long-running shell command as a background terminal (executed via the platform shell — sh -c on POSIX, cmd.exe /d /s /c on Windows). Fire-and-forget: this returns immediately with an id, and you get a message with the final output when the process exits. The process receives NO stdin (immediate EOF) and there is no way to send input later — interactive commands will not work; use bg_kill to stop a stuck one. Terminals are session-scoped: they are killed when the session ends or reloads. Output shown to you is tail-truncated (stdout 16.0KB, stderr 8.0KB); the full logs are captured to files and in the /ps viewer. Max 8 background terminals can run at once.

Codemode: `tools.bg_start(args)` resolves to a string.

command.description: Shell command line to run in the background (sh -c on POSIX, cmd.exe /d /s /c on Windows). It receives no stdin (EOF immediately); interactive commands will not work.

title.description: Short human-readable name shown in listings and the UI

toolsAdded.name: bg_status
toolsAdded.description:
Peek at a background terminal's status and current output (tail-truncated) without blocking. If the terminal already exited, this returns its final state.

Codemode: `tools.bg_status(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: bg_list
toolsAdded.description:
List all background terminals (running and settled) with pid, elapsed time, exit status, and output sizes.

Codemode: `tools.bg_list(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: bg_kill
toolsAdded.description:
Stop one or more running background terminals (SIGTERM to the whole process tree, escalating to SIGKILL). Returns each terminal's final state; already-settled ids are reported as such.

Codemode: `tools.bg_kill(args)` resolves to a string.

toolsAdded.name: subagent
toolsAdded.description:
One child: {agent,task}. Independent parallel children: {workflow:"parallel",args:{tasks:[{agent,task},...]}}. Dependent multi-step work: exactly one top-level subagent workflow call with async:true; write one ```js workflow block in this reply, then call subagent({workflow:true}); children launch only inside it.
Management: {action,id?,options:{...}}; fields not in this schema go in options.
Launch agents by name and pass models as exact provider/id; an unknown agent or model returns the valid choices.
Details: guide workflows/recommended-orchestration-pattern (async, review, failure recovery), guide workflows/scripted-workflows, guide tool-reference/retained-children, guide tool-reference/external-cli-agent-profiles.

SAFETY-CRITICAL SUBAGENT GUIDANCE:
- Delegate only when the operator asked, directly or through applicable user/project instructions; size, complexity or risk alone is not authorization.
- Native async completion wakes this session: return control; do not sleep, poll or call bg_wait for it.
- One writer per cwd/worktree; isolate concurrent writers.
- After a launch or runtime failure, stop and report it; never silently switch to interactive_shell, pi -ne or another CLI.

workflow.description: true: run the one ```js workflow block written in this same reply (false invalid). String with '/': script file read from request cwd. Other string: named workflow resource. Raw scripts (true or path) have no runs.host.

args.description: Plain-JSON args for workflow; 16 fields/object, 64 items/array, depth 8, 16 KiB total; raw-script args are exposed deeply frozen and persisted, so do not include secrets.

async.description: Background; default asyncByDefault. false only to block parent.

model.description: Child model provider/id; bare id only if unique. Suffix :off/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max overrides agent thinking default.

worktree.description: Isolate each workflow child in a managed git worktree; child worktree:false overrides default.

output.description: Child output path or false; relative workflow paths use managed artifact routing. Bind durable output here, not task prose; return outputReference/outputPathMapping/artifactPaths.

action.description: Management/control only; omit for execution. validate accepts workflow: true or a script path. Discover actions with {action:"guide",options:{topic:"tool-reference"}}.

options.description: Every field not listed here, such as acceptance, timeoutMs, context, view and index; guide tool-reference/parameter-reference.

toolsAdded.name: contact_supervisor
toolsAdded.description: Contact the parent/supervisor session for a blocking decision, structured interview, or progress update.

toolsAdded.name: bg_wait
toolsAdded.description:
Wait for background work, then return. Ordinary async subagent runs already wake this session natively; use bg_wait only for provider, detached, or other background work without native notification, when a same-turn result is needed.
{} — first active run or provider item to finish or need attention.
{all:true} — all work active at call time.
{id} — one run; a finished async run returns its result references.
{id,nonBlocking:true} — subscribe to that run's wake and return now.
Timeout or a user message ends the wait without error; work keeps running.

Codemode: `tools.bg_wait(args)` resolves to a string.

nonBlocking.description: Subscribe to id's wake and return immediately; requires id, not with all.

all.description: Wait for all work active at call time.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait; default waitTool.defaultTimeoutMs, then 30 min.

stopOnAttention.description: false: keep waiting through idle or long-thinking attention.

toolsAdded.name: subagent_supervisor
toolsAdded.description: Native pi-subagents supervisor channel. Use reply/pending/status to answer child subagent requests without overriding pi-intercom.

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /Users/sofianebebert/.local/share/mise/installs/pi/1.3.0/pi/docs/codemode.md first.

8:build workflow    scout → plan → implement (single writer, checked acceptance handoff)

# Factory (`/factory`)

A minimal, reliable software factory. `/factory <task>` launches a bounded, asynchronous software-delivery pipeline and keeps the parent Pi session as the orchestrator.

## Pipeline

```
build workflow    scout → plan → implement (single writer, checked acceptance handoff)
deterministic     human-authored validation commands from .pi/factory.json
review workflow   3 parallel fresh reviewers (correctness, tests, simplicity)
                  → at most ONE fix pass, only on structured "fix" verdicts
deterministic     the same trusted commands, rerun as final verification
```

- Scout, planner, and reviewers run with fresh context and read-only toolsets; the implement and fix workers are the only writers (one at a time).
- Every machine-consumed child result uses a structured output schema, and branching happens **only** on the structured verdict — never on reviewer prose.
- The plan or implement stage stopping with unresolved human-owned decisions pauses the factory (`needs_approval`) instead of proceeding.
- Malformed or missing structured output fails the stage closed (`needs_attention`), never onward as success.
- The fix loop is capped at exactly one pass by construction. Failed deterministic checks also stop the factory — no automated retry of side-effectful work.

  # Factory (`/factory`)
  A minimal, reliable software factory. `/factory <task>` launches a bounded, asynchronous software-delivery pipeline and keeps the parent Pi session as the orchestrator.
  ## Pipeline
  ```
  build workflow    scout → plan → implement (single writer, checked acceptance handoff)
  deterministic     human-authored validation commands from .pi/factory.json
  review workflow   3 parallel fresh reviewers (correctness, tests, simplicity)
                    → at most ONE fix pass, only on structured "fix" verdicts
  deterministic     the same trusted commands, rerun as final verification
  ```
  - Scout, planner, and reviewers run with fresh context and read-only toolsets; the implement and fix workers are the only writers (one at a time).
  - Every machine-consumed child result uses a structured output schema, and branching happens **only** on the structured verdict — never on reviewer prose.
  - The plan or implement stage stopping with unresolved human-owned decisions pauses the factory (`needs_approval`) instead of proceeding.
  - Malformed or missing structured output fails the stage closed (`needs_attention`), never onward as success.
  - Writers report through pi-subagents' `structured_output` tool with two channels kept strictly separate: the `value` object carries the full handoff schema (`changedFiles`, `implementationSummary`, `commandsRun` with exit codes, `testsAddedOrUpdated`, `residualRisks`, `workLeftUndone`, `decisionsRequiringApproval`), while the `acceptanceReport` object may contain only pi-subagents' supported fields (`changedFiles`, `testsAddedOrUpdated`, `commandsRun` as `{command, result, summary}`, `residualRisks`, `validationOutput`, `noStagedFiles`, `diffSummary`, `reviewFindings`, `manualNotes`) — unsupported fields such as `workLeftUndone` are rejected there and would fail the worker at the acceptance handoff.
  - The fix loop is capped at exactly one pass by construction. Failed deterministic checks also stop the factory — no automated retry of side-effectful work.
  - **No commit, push, merge, publish, deploy, or release is ever performed.**
  Execution, lifecycle, missions, artifacts, status, resume, and Herdr integration are owned by the installed [pi-subagents](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents) package; this extension only validates the baseline, generates the two fixed workflows, correlates RPC replies, and runs the deterministic checks.
  ## Commands
  | Command | Purpose |
  | --- | --- |
  | `/factory <task>` | Validate trust/baseline/config, then launch the build workflow asynchronously. |
  | `/factory-status` | Show the latest run: swimlane waterfall, live workflow state, checks, reviewer disposition, decisions, errors. |
  Baseline requirements: trusted project, inside a git work tree, clean working tree (unless `allowDirtyBaseline` is enabled), and `.pi/factory.json` present and valid.
  ## Configuration — `.pi/factory.json`
  Human-authored project configuration. It is the **only** source of validation commands the factory will ever execute; commands proposed by model output are never run. Unknown fields and malformed values fail closed.
  ```json
  {
    "version": 1,
    "validationCommands": [
      { "name": "test", "command": "pnpm test" },
      { "name": "typecheck", "command": "pnpm run typecheck" }
    ],
    "timeoutMs": 1800000,
    "commandTimeoutMs": 300000,
    "maxConcurrency": 4,
    "allowDirtyBaseline": false
  }
  ```
  | Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `version` | `1` | required | Schema version, exactly `1`. |
  | `validationCommands` | `{name, command}[]` (1–8) | required | Trusted validation commands, run in order between workflow phases and again as final verification. Single-line, ≤ 4096 chars each. |
  | `timeoutMs` | integer 60 000–86 400 000 | `1800000` | Workflow deadline for each factory workflow launch. |
  | `commandTimeoutMs` | integer 1 000–3 600 000 | `300000` | Per-command timeout for validation checks. |
  | `maxConcurrency` | integer 1–16 | `4` | Upper bound passed to pi-subagents as the workflow's global concurrency limit. |
  | `allowDirtyBaseline` | boolean | `false` | Allow launching from a dirty git baseline. |
  Never place prompts, credentials, secrets, or shell fragments from model output in this file.
  ## Deliberate deviation: checks run in the extension, not via `runs.host`
  pi-subagents 0.61 grants `runs.host` authority only to named workflow resources (currently `npm test` / `npm run typecheck`); inline workflow scripts launched through the public execution boundary (`script` RPC param) cannot use it. The factory therefore runs the trusted validation commands **in this extension process**, between the two workflows, using strictly-validated human-authored configuration with bounded timeouts and output capture. The security property is preserved: model-proposed commands are never executed, and the commands come only from `.pi/factory.json`.
  If a future pi-subagents version exposes a user/project workflow-resource registry, the check phase can migrate to `runs.host` without changing the pipeline shape.
  ## Live waterfall UX
  Instead of a flat text dump, a run is rendered as a **swimlane waterfall**: one bar per pipeline lane (scout, plan, implement, checks, review ×3, fix, final checks) on a shared time axis, colored by state (accent = running, success = done, error = failed, warning = paused).
  - A widget above the editor shows the chart for the latest run and updates live: the active lane grows toward "now" and the current sub-stage appears in the status bar (`factory: build · implement`).
  - Sub-stage spans come from a 3s poll of the pi-subagents `status` RPC (`Workflow child <key>: … <status>` lines). Coarse phase spans (build/checks/review/final) are always recorded exactly at phase transitions, so the chart degrades gracefully when polling is unavailable; fine sub-spans replace their coarse span at render time.
  - Spans are stored as milliseconds relative to the run start in the session entry, so the waterfall survives restarts and branch restores (fail-closed validation rejects malformed spans).
  - When a run finishes, the widget keeps the final chart and the completion notification stays short (task, verdict, final checks, changed files); `/factory-status` renders the full waterfall plus all details.
  - Layout and status parsing live in `src/waterfall.ts` as pure, unit-tested functions; the widget component (`WaterfallWidget`) only reads the shared model and applies theme colors.
  ## Tests
  ```bash
  pnpm test   # or: node --experimental-strip-types --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning --test tests/factory/*.test.ts
  ```
  Covers: strict config validation, safe task encoding (quotes, Markdown fences, shell-like text, multiline prompts), sandboxed execution of the generated workflows (stage order, structured-verdict-only branching, bounded fix pass, fail-closed malformed output), deterministic check execution, RPC request/reply correlation and timeouts, waterfall layout/round-trip (`waterfall.test.ts`), and offline validation of both generated scripts against the **real** installed `validateWorkflowScript` plus a read-only smoke test against the **real** RPC bridge. # Research: pi-subagents acceptance rejection and async resume

## Summary

For **pi-subagents v0.61.0**, `acceptance: "checked"` is a structured-evidence gate, not merely a child-process exit check. Rejection means acceptance evaluation failed—e.g. absent/invalid report, required evidence missing, a structural check failing, or required review failing. Tagged docs say unknown/ambiguous report keys or enum values fail with field-level diagnostics. There is **no documented automatic retry triggered by acceptance rejection**; any retry must be explicit workflow/parent logic. Explicit verification-command gates belong to stricter `verified` acceptance, not every `checked` run.

Async run artifacts persist, but an event notification is not a durable message queue. The extension RPC advertises `events.asyncComplete` as **process-local completion correlation after spawn**. Docs say session shutdown disposes its completion watcher; detached work can finish without notifying anyone. Current workflows docs say same-process `/resume` transfers async-run ownership and completion notices, but a process restart/another Pi process is not guaranteed to inherit that ownership. For reliable recovery, persist the returned run id and reconcile/poll package `status` (targeted status / async snapshot or canonical run status files) after resume/startup rather than relying on replay of an old event.

**Confidence:** high on documented acceptance checks and process-local notification boundary; medium on exact recovery/replay behavior across v0.61 because current workflows docs give stronger same-process resume semantics than v0.61 observability docs, and no event replay/catch-up contract was found. The truncated error suffix cannot identify which predicate failed.

## Findings

### 1. `Acceptance rejected` under `checked`

- **Direct evidence (v0.61.0 tool reference):** Acceptance levels include `checked`; `evidenceStatus: "rejected"` means “attestation, structural checks, verification, or review failed.” For `checked`, runtime structural checks include required evidence and no staged files. Structured acceptance report is requested at attested-or-stricter levels.
- **Direct evidence:** “The parser canonicalizes known enum synonyms, snake_case report keys and wrappers, underscore fence tags, unambiguous scalar arrays, string booleans, and criterion-id separators. Unknown or ambiguous keys and enum values fail with field-level diagnostics. Explicit empty `changedFiles` and `testsAddedOrUpdated` arrays are recorded as not applicable; missing fields and empty required command or validation evidence still fail.”
- **Direct evidence:** “Explicit failed gates fail the run. Inferred gates remain observable without failing the run.” A configured host verification (`verify`/`gate`) is a `verified` acceptance feature; do not infer that every `checked` run executes tests.
- **Watchdog distinction:** Required acceptance review failure/blockers can reject acceptance. A **watchdog** finding is not named among the acceptance rejection criteria inspected; watchdog is documented as a separate second-model monitor. Treat watchdog blockers as separate unless workflow wiring explicitly makes them an acceptance/review gate. Automatic mapping: **not confirmed**.
- **Incident interpretation:** `Acceptance rejected: Failed to p…` is consistent with report parse/validation or missing required evidence, but the truncation cannot distinguish missing report, unknown/ambiguous field, missing evidence, staged changes, configured gate, or review failure. Full diagnostic and run record needed.
- **Retry/run outcome:** No acceptance-specific automatic retry is documented. A rejected child is returned as failed/rejected; outer workflow logic may handle a result or decide whether siblings continue. Changelog recovery such as one-time auto-resume after setup-phase abort with zero usage is a different failure class, not acceptance retry.

**Source:** [`docs/tool-reference.md` v0.61.0](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/blob/v0.61.0/docs/tool-reference.md#acceptance-gates), snapshot hash `694606cf324d99b6440f5212517d57369a6047308358522414ceca41a365cb0d`; section offsets 34,439–44,037 (parser/failed-gate excerpt at 38,439–44,037).

**History/qualification:** [Issue #451](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/issues/451) reports a historical false rejection where a configured output file held a structured report but acceptance was evaluated from the final assistant text: “the parent can still receive `Acceptance rejected: Structured acceptance report not found`.” Its proposed fix was to evaluate acceptance against the same authoritative raw output as the deliverable. Relevant when using explicit/file-only outputs; do not assume this historical bug explains the present case. The v0.61.0 changelog says it “Preserve[d] durable file-only child reports and continue[d] read-only workflow review after malformed acceptance metadata (#1724).”

**Sources:** [`CHANGELOG.md` v0.61.0](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/blob/v0.61.0/CHANGELOG.md), hash `9d4adf59c2d9c55cb3d9dfe94f2f281aeca76c6de3055427d2c958fa36d469c2`, offsets 0–2,244; [issue #451](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/issues/451), hash `edeb4ee9b25a59db82b698287be1c4eca96026a00d6ea3efd9a20d59f769a4c6`, offsets 4,000+.

### 2. Async persistence, resume, and completion correlation

- **Direct evidence (v0.61.0 extension API):** RPC methods include `status`, `spawn`, and `resume`. `status` replies retain `details` and, when available, `asyncSnapshot`; `resume` uses the revival path and validates current-session ownership, persisted session/recovery metadata, stopped/live state, capabilities, and exclusive session lease. `ping` advertises `events.asyncComplete` as “exact process-local completion correlation after RPC `spawn`.” This is not a durable replay promise.
- **Direct evidence (extension host/session notes):** Ordinary completion wakes use a result watcher/notifier; “Session shutdown stops the result watcher and disposes this completion notifier.” “Detached children do not stop when the session does. They are the host process's children, not the session's, so the run keeps going, completes, and notifies nobody. What is lost is the notification, not the work.” Docs recommend reading async status files, treating `queued`/`running` as live, and not interpreting stale `lastUpdate` as a heartbeat.
- **Direct evidence (current workflows docs, not pinned v0.61):** After `/new`, `/resume`, or fork **in the same Pi process**, the replacement session owns async runs from replaced session(s), can list/`bg_wait`/control them, and receives notices. “Startup and other Pi processes inherit nothing.” A stopped-by-runtime-replacement workflow can be relaunched with `options: { reuseFrom: "<stopped run id>" }` under constraints. This is workflow reuse, not general replay of an already-fired completion event.
- **Re-delivery answer:** No document promises an already-fired `asyncComplete` event is re-emitted to an extension listener after resume. Same-process Pi session resume has documented ownership/wakeup behavior in current docs; process restart does not inherit that notification ownership. Treat durable run status as truth and poll/reconcile.
- **`bg_wait`:** v0.61 changelog makes `bg_wait` the primary background-work wait tool and `subagent_wait` a deprecated compatibility alias. Docs distinguish the wait-subscription path from ordinary completion wakes; no event replay/catch-up guarantee is stated.
- **`async-retention` / orphan recovery:** No public v0.61 contract guaranteeing an `async-retention` setting, indefinite completed-run retention, or a generic orphan-recovery operation that replays missed RPC completion events was found. Artifacts/status persist, but retention duration for this installed version remains unconfirmed.

**Sources:** [`docs/extension-api.md` v0.61.0](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/blob/v0.61.0/docs/extension-api.md#in-process-event-bus-rpc), hash `acafdecdcf57e1980b3ddcad5a65c399d9d1a8d4ed202a0c02f7fda7cddbaeeb`, offsets 0–3,659 (RPC/methods), 3,682–7,682 (`asyncSnapshot` and process-local scope), and 27,759–31,759 (host lifetime); [`docs/workflows.md` current](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/blob/main/docs/workflows.md), hash `a9f07c33d6ebd4be8f2a643941ebb07ca799cdecd1b7d1c57a1b11f6c1bb86c3`, offsets 3,651–7,651 (current-main resume semantics); [`CHANGELOG.md` v0.61.0](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/blob/v0.61.0/CHANGELOG.md), hash above, offsets 0–2,244 (`bg_wait`).

### 3. Live progress and extension-parent limitations

- **Direct evidence:** `pi.events` is in-process-only and “does not reach separate Pi processes or child subagents”; docs direct cross-process coordination to lifecycle artifacts or `pi-intercom`.
- **Direct evidence:** RPC `status` supports targeted/rich reads and successful replies can include `asyncSnapshot`; targeted status stays executor-backed. This is the documented reconciliation surface, not an event replay API.
- **Direct evidence (observability):** Background runs are inspectable with `subagent({ action: "status" })` or by id and visible in Pi progress/status/fleet surfaces. Successful completion can be quiet in inactive tabs, while failed/paused completions notify the originating session; that UI behavior is not a promise to arbitrary extension listeners.
- **Implication:** Store the RPC spawn run id durably and subscribe to `asyncComplete` for low-latency live updates, but reconcile that id through `status` on session start/resume and after missed events. Persist terminal state/output/error in the parent extension. On process restart, verify status/artifact access; persistence of run artifacts does not imply inherited session ownership.

**Sources:** [`docs/extension-api.md` v0.61.0](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/blob/v0.61.0/docs/extension-api.md), hash above, offsets 3,682–7,682 and 27,759–31,759; [`docs/observability.md` v0.61.0](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/blob/v0.61.0/docs/observability.md), hash `adc34ea585d37f9cc2fa97005e6db88b0dcf6fbf0511c56610711559f576f667`, offsets 0–4,000 and 1,815–5,815. `async-complete` here means the documented `events.asyncComplete` capability, not a separately confirmed persistent event queue.

## Contradictions

- Not a direct contradiction: current workflow docs describe same-process session ownership/notifications; the extension API bounds RPC event correlation as process-local and says host shutdown disposes the notifier. This distinguishes Pi run ownership/wakeup on same-process resume from replay to a newly installed listener or process. No doc promises replay of a finished run's event.
- Issue #451 documents a historical report-source false rejection. v0.61 changelog recognizes durable file-only reports and malformed metadata, but the exact fix coverage for the user's installed patch level is not established here.

- Error is truncated; need the full rejection diagnostic, per-run acceptance ledger/report, status/receipt, and structured-output result (if used) to identify the failing gate.
- No public v0.61 `async-retention` duration/setting or guarantee of indefinite completed-status retention found.

- Deprioritized: provider snippets (discovery only), unrelated issue #440 (obsolete `reviewed` level), and latest releases/README as evidence for v0.61 behavior.

One-letter token mismatch: successful lanes aggregate to `"queued"`, `setSpanState` runs, `endMs` stays `null` forever.

If the completion event isn't delivered, a restored active phase polls forever with cosmetic updates and can never reach a terminal state.
- Two event-loss/freeze vectors: (a) completion ownership is **per-process** (`completion-owner.js:5–7`) — a quit-and-reopen resume gets a new owner id and pi-subagents skips the persisted result (`result-watcher.js:226`), losing the event; (b) once any terminal branch runs, `stopPolling()` + status-line blanking intentionally freeze everything — so even the "correct" failed path looks dead.
- **Failed runs have no recovery path**: no retry command; every terminal branch calls `stopPolling()`; the only continuation is rerunning `/factory` fresh (allowed, since `failed` isn't in `ACTIVE_PHASES`). The factory never calls pi-subagents' `resume`/`manage` RPC.
